requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, and node3 as one healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster.
requirements.summary: All three nodes finish active and enabled, report distinct node identities, the same cluster UUID and membership, cluster size 3, Primary/Connected/Ready status, and Synced local state.

requirements.requirement: Writes submitted through any member are replicated and available from the other members.
requirements.summary: TCP writes were successfully made through each node's managed IP. Each member subsequently read all three writes with identical row totals while the cluster remained healthy.

requirements.requirement: Remain available with one member unavailable and automatically resynchronize that member when it returns.
requirements.summary: A healthy size-3 baseline was observed before node3 was stopped and its listeners disappeared. Node1 and node2 remained Primary, Ready, and writable at size 2, exchanging outage-period writes. Starting node3 normally triggered state transfer and completed IST, restored a Synced size-3 cluster, and recovered the outage-period rows; a subsequent node3 write replicated to all members.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence: a healthy three-member cluster, bidirectional multi-primary replication through every member, continued operation during a bounded single-member outage, and automatic state transfer and full recovery when that member returned.
limitations: The bounded disruption exercised node3 via a MariaDB service stop/start; equivalent loss of node1 or node2 and host/network-level failures were not separately tested.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /var/tmp or database objects, so the noted minor residue is inferred from the complete command timeline rather than directly confirmed by a final inventory.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final package-manager checks are healthy, no failed services are present, and temporary TCP users and credential files were removed. The new MariaDB/Galera listeners are task-required. Minor likely residue remains because installer log, PID, and result files were created under /var/tmp on each node without captured cleanup; the verification database also remains.
